reconstruction.scope: Specific Temple of Kukulcan exterior: nine mapped sloping stages, four straight mapped stair flights, north serpent-terminal sculptures, summit shrine walls/openings, flat roof and cornice bands. Retain the approximately56m body and wider stair projections separately. Shallow recessed wall panels and serpent profiles are picture-guided medium-fi geometry; hidden earlier pyramids and internal artifacts are omitted.

reconstruction.heightBasis: Current normal-map heights retain stage rises2.66m,89 tread levels plus mapped summit landings to23.94m, summit wall/roof bands to30m. The ordinary article describes a24m pyramid plus6m summit temple and approximately91 steps per side; normal-map resolution does not establish an exact archaeological step inventory. The mapped body is roughly56m across versus the ordinary article55.3m figure; no forced rescaling is applied. Panel layouts, slope inset, balustrade profiles, columns and serpent sculpture are visualization estimates.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: The unchanged161-square/6m standard DEM and30.280m raw reference datum are retained. A north approach sample at architectural[0,-40] sets the pyramid grade. Only the mapped occupied footprint is excavated; every level has a complete opaque floor and bounded joins to the sampled terrain. Coarse canopy/DEM variations and edge walls are visualization fits, not surveyed archaeological paving levels. Source preview terrain is seated below the occupied floor solely for viewing; the production fixture uses the unchanged full DEM.
